features.name: New plan traffic starts at zero; local-node usage never re-counts remote traffic
features.description: Two causes of phantom usage (prod case doriswangqi@outlook.com: 18.5 GB shown right after a renewal on 2026-10-02). (1) The cycle window summed whole China days from the cycle-start day, so traffic from earlier on the purchase day (and before a 30-day rollover instant) counted against the new cycle. Purchases and rollovers now open a cycle baseline (user.xuiTrafficCycleBaseline) that is settled by the first sampling round whose counter reads started after the purchase/rollover instant; cycle usage = window sums minus the baseline, so the new plan starts at exactly zero (traffic within at most one sampling round after purchase is given to the customer). (2) The local panel node (LA BWH) derived its usage as max(0, Δglobal − ΣΔremote) per round: a failed remote read, a transient dip of the panel's global counter, or global read lag moved remote traffic onto LA (prod: LA 15.2 GB in one day vs ~0.16 GB real lifetime). The sampler now uses xuiTraffic.localNodeRound: signed global and remote growth with a carried deficit stored on the local cursor (carry_up/carry_down), and the local node is held while any configured remote node is unreadable.

features.name: Mail the user when traffic reaches 100%
features.description: When the five-minute panel sync finds an active self-hosted user at or over the quota (the round that disables the client), the user is mailed 流量已用完，服务已暂停 with used and total traffic, the next reset date when it falls before the plan ends, and how to resume. It is switched by alertSettings.traffic.userDepletedMail (on by default; stored settings without the field read as on) from 流量用尽邮件提醒 in 通用设置 → 提醒设置, separately from the threshold mail. Only users who reach the quota in the current round are mailed: the previous round's ledger (weightedBytes against totalBytes) must have been under the quota, so users already used up when the feature ships or when the switch is turned on get nothing, and a raised quota that is still used up is not a new depletion. A failed send is kept as pending under cycleKey:depleted in the ledger and retried in the following rounds; a user who tops up, is seen under the quota, and uses it up again is mailed again. Expired or disabled users are skipped, and nothing is sent in XUI_READ_ONLY mode because the client is not actually paused.

features.name: node-hub controls xboard-node on every VPS
features.description: node-hub/ is a loopback service that speaks Xboard's node API to unmodified xboard-node (machine mode, per-machine tokens, ETag/304) and an internal API to server.js. The app pushes per-user entitlements (uuid, node ids from line groups and personal custom inbounds, speed limit, device limit, enabled) every 60s and on every provisioning change; node reports land as per-user deltas in xui_daily_traffic (node_guid hub-m<machine>, deduplicated by report id), so weighted billing, depletion, daily charts and profitability are unchanged. Hub nodes appear as inbounds (key hub-m<machine>:<node>, id 1e9+node) in inbound management, line groups, set-enable, settings, presence, monitor and subscriptions, and are never sent to 3x-ui. Works next to 3x-ui (reusing the 3x-ui uuid) or alone (hub-only billing job). scripts/migrate-xui-to-node-hub.js moves one 3x-ui VPS. Nothing runs when NODE_HUB_URL is unset.
done_criteria: Unmodified xboard-node pulls config and users from node-hub and its traffic is billed within 5% of the bytes transferred.
Speed limit, device limit, depletion, re-enable and node disable reach the node.
Hub nodes work in line groups, inbound settings, custom inbounds, presence, monitor and subscriptions, alone or next to 3x-ui.
With node-hub unconfigured, existing 3x-ui behavior and tests are unchanged.

features.name: node-hub pushes changes to xboard-node over WebSocket
features.description: node-hub/push.js speaks Xboard's Workerman WebSocket protocol. The handshake advertises ws_url (<NODE_HUB_PUBLIC_URL>/api/v2/server/ws) unless NODE_HUB_WEBSOCKET=false; a machine connects once with its token and stops polling config and users. Each connection keeps per-node hashes of what it received and a reconcile (200 ms after any management write, plus every 30 s) pushes sync.nodes, sync.config, sync.users and sync.devices (global device IPs from report.devices). A node that loses its last user gets sync.user.delta 'resync' in machine mode (xboard-node's machine mailbox drops an emptied list, an unknown action makes it reconcile over REST) and 'remove' in node mode. Revoked credentials close the socket; app-level ping every 30 s, idle sockets dropped after 90 s. Traffic, presence and machine status stay on REST. The admin Node Hub page shows 实时推送 / 轮询 per machine and the push setting on the overview.
done_criteria: A stock xboard-node in machine mode connects to the push channel and receives node, config and user changes without polling.
Removing a node's last user, depletion, re-enable and node disable reach the node within seconds with REST polling stretched to 5 minutes.
Revoked machine credentials close the connection; REST polling keeps working when push is off.
The admin page shows which machines hold a push channel.

features.name: Per-user node source (3xui / nodehub / mix) for side-by-side migration
features.description: Self-hosted users get a 设置节点来源 action in the user detail page's 管理用户 list that opens a dialog (PUT /api/users/:id/node-source); the profile card shows 节点来源 under 钱包余额. mix (default, not stored) puts both 3x-ui panel nodes and node-hub nodes in /sub; 3xui keeps only panel nodes; nodehub keeps only hub nodes. It only filters the subscription: the user stays provisioned and entitled on both sides, and traffic from either architecture is booked into xui_daily_traffic and billed. Changes are recorded in the user log. scripts/migrate-xui-to-node-hub.js gains --port-offset <n> (hub nodes listen on 3x-ui port + n so 3x-ui's xray keeps running on the same VPS) and --add-to-line-groups (adds hub keys next to the 3x-ui keys instead of replacing them).
